comparison: Perfect agreement on cost-effectiveness claims (C12, C96, C97). Both evaluations find the system rivals commercial instruments at a fraction of the cost. OpenEval notes lack of detailed cost breakdown, while peer reviewers accept the cost comparison without question.

Perfect agreement on objective cost limitations (C100-C103). Both evaluations acknowledge the high-NA objective as the main cost barrier and accept the necessity of expensive optics for scientific imaging quality.

Strong agreement on single-particle tracking capabilities (C9, C10, C76-C78, C80). Both find the quantum dot tracking data convincing. OpenEval provides detailed validation of experimental support, peer reviewers explicitly list this among convincing demonstrations.

Strong agreement on super-resolution imaging (C11, C81-C84). Both evaluations confirm STORM capability with convincing experimental data. OpenEval validates FRC resolution measurements, peer reviewers accept the super-resolution quality without concerns.

Agreement on software integration (C55-C58, C137-C138). Peer reviewers explicitly praise the tight hardware-software integration as a strength. OpenEval notes lack of experimental validation for drift compensation and Napari plugin, but peer reviewers do not raise these concerns.

Agreement on long-term live-cell imaging (C8, C72-C75). Both evaluations confirm the system successfully performs extended imaging in incubators. OpenEval validates with Figure 4 data, peer reviewers explicitly affirm this capability.

Divergent evaluations on accessibility claims (C13, C98). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of empirical evidence from lay users. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the system makes microscopy accessible to broader audiences.

Divergent evaluations on potential applications (C14, C15). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of deployment evidence in resource-limited settings. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the work will enable broader access and remove obstacles.
Agreement on live-cell imaging and stability (C68-C71). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval validates with Figure 3 data, peer reviewers confirm extended live-cell imaging as convincing.

Agreement on drift measurements (C66, C67). OpenEval validates with Figure 2d bead tracking data. Peer reviewers implicitly accept stability claims as part of the convincing experimental package without explicit discussion.

Agreement on core microscope design and documentation (C6, C30-C32, C34, C40, C85-C87). Both evaluations find the UC2 framework expansion well-documented with compelling evidence. OpenEval covers broader claim set including detailed component specifications.

Agreement on widefield imaging quality (C63-C65, C161). Both evaluations find the illumination and imaging data convincing. OpenEval validates with Figure 2 measurements, peer reviewers explicitly affirm the experimental data quality.

Divergent evaluations on future capabilities (C93, C112). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative claims without experimental demonstration. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing educational and accessibility potential positively.

Agreement on component selection and cost factors (C44-C47, C49). Both evaluations accept the camera cost comparison and component choices. Peer reviewers explicitly note the combination of cheap and expensive components.

Divergent evaluations on injection molding (C90-C92). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED without concerns. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether limited availability of injection-molded blocks limits the open-source accessibility.

OpenEval evaluates optical design principles (C35-C39) as SUPPORTED but notes lack of experimental validation for troubleshooting advantages. Peer reviewers focus on injection molding accessibility concerns (C90-C92) rather than optical design principles.
OpenEval evaluates background and literature context claims (C1-C5, C16-C29, C113-C114) as SUPPORTED with proper citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological claims for cell culture and sample preparation (C152-C160) as SUPPORTED, following standard protocols. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methods.
